plan_items.title: Ingest the state monument-commission corpus in priority order: New York Final Report, Pennsylvania at Gettysburg, then Maine/NJ/Michigan/Minnesota and small states
plan_items.evidence: Measured site coverage: NY 75 + PA 74 = 149 of 570 unit records (26%). IA: finalreportongettys01burgrich (vol.1, 548 imgs, 1,435,851 bytes, NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT; text states 'sixty-eight New York regiments or battalions of infantry present' and 'nineteen New York batteries'); pennsylvaniaatge05penn (1893 v1, 638 imgs) + pennsgettysburg01reynrich/02reynrich (1914 v1-2) + pennsylvaniaatg03penn (v3); maineatgettysbu01commgoog (701 imgs, 1.6 MB); finalreportofget00newj + newjerseytroopsi00intoom (NJ); cu31924030924736 (Michigan 1889); minnesotacivil01minnrich; small volumes for VT/MD/IL/IN/RI/VA/OH/CT (13-370 KB each). Gaps (no dedicated book found): WI, MA (only Roe 1910), DE, NH, WV, Confederate states.
plan_items.root_cause: State commissions collected veteran-written regimental histories, inscriptions and dedication speeches in the 1880s-1910s; none of this narrative depth exists in the site's 467 one-line 'key_action' strings (e.g. U-20ME carries a 2-3 sentence key_action string and a flag_notes line).
plan_items.fix: Per book: (1) canonical edition pick (PA: 1914 superset; NY: vol.1 Fox narrative + per-regiment sketches + vol.3 monument data); (2) segment by regiment heading using the book's own contents page + the alias table; (3) emit sections.jsonl {doc_id, unit_id, section_type: narrative|address|inscription|roster, author, year, text, page}; (4) attach provenance tag 'veteran_memory_1893' etc.; (5) store editions as variants, dedupe by normalized-text hash. Do NY and PA first (149 units), then ME/NJ/MI/MN (35 units), then the small volumes as whole documents with unit tags.
plan_items.acceptance_test: Every NY and PA unit record has >= 1 narrative section linked (target 90%); 25 spot-checked sections reproduce the printed page text; each section has ia_id + leaf + printed page; unit coverage report lists units without a state-book section.
plan_items.metric_or_grade_moved: Content depth for 75-149+ regiments; historian answer quality for unit-specific questions

plan_items.title: Replace copyrighted-compilation provenance in the OOB data with a PD-derived casualty/strength table (OR returns + Fox + Phisterer + Dyer + Livermore) and a documented reconciliation policy
plan_items.evidence: deploy/data/oob/union_regiments_i_ii_corps.json metadata.sources lists Busey & Martin (Longstreet House 1994), Pfanz (UNC Press 1987/2001), Hessler & Motts (Savas Beatie 2015), Moe (1993), Desjardin (1995). Unit records carry strength, casualties and (for some) casualty_percentage fields. Fox (1889) IA reglossescivilwar00foxwrich (2,255,231 bytes; NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT) but its OCR tables contain digit errors ('(5,024', '30S', '000', '4,2 lo'), so raw scraping is unsafe; OR27-1 No.13 (Return of Casualties at Gettysburg) and No.15 (general return), OR27-2 No.427 (Guild) are the PD primaries.
plan_items.root_cause: Numbers were compiled from secondary books; facts are not copyrightable but a curated compilation may be, and the site cannot show per-number provenance or explain why sources differ.
plan_items.fix: Build casualty_sources.jsonl with one row per (unit_id, source, killed, wounded, missing, total, strength) for OR returns, Fox, Phisterer, Dyer, Livermore (aggregates). Parse Fox tables by rebuilding columns (hOCR word boxes or row-sum checksum: K+W+M must equal total +/-0), reject rows failing the checksum into a manual queue. Publish a reconciliation column set (or_value, fox_value, site_value, delta, note) and a rule: site value = OR return where present, else Fox, else Dyer; keep Busey/Martin only as 'see also' after counsel review. Add 'source' badge to unit cards.
plan_items.acceptance_test: For 100% of units with an OR return or Fox row, site casualties == rule value; checksum failures < 3% after manual queue; a diff report lists all units where OR and Fox differ by > 10% with explanation; oob files' metadata.sources no longer lists copyrighted books as the numeric source.
plan_items.metric_or_grade_moved: Legal/provenance risk; data accuracy (C4/H10 class); trust

plan_items.title: Ingest participant narratives (Battles & Leaders v3, SHSP v1-43, Joint Committee v1, Haskell/Oates/Curtis/Holcombe/Polley) with mandatory perspective/bias tags
plan_items.evidence: IA battlesleadersof03john (786 imgs, 3,251,232 bytes, OCR proxy 0.966) - OCR contents lists ~25 Gettysburg articles pp.244-~440 (Longstreet 244, Hunt 255/290/369, Gibbon 313, Melcher 314 '20th Maine at Little Round Top', Law 318, Kershaw 331, Alexander 357...). SHSP vols 1-43: 49.0 MB, 2,949 'Gettysburg' mentions; densest vols 4 (312), 37 (253), 5 (204). Joint Committee v1 (reportofjointcomm01unit): 345 'Gettysburg' / 212 'Sickles' mentions; witness headings include Meade, Warren, Sickles, Howe, Birney, Doubleday, Pleasonton, Hancock, Butterfield, Gibbon, Hunt. Curtis 24th Michigan: 549 Gettysburg mentions.
plan_items.root_cause: Contested postwar narratives (Longstreet/Early-Allan, Sickles vs Meade) will be presented as neutral fact by a keyword retriever unless each passage carries author, date written, side and controversy tags.
plan_items.fix: Schema fields: perspective {side:'union|confederate|civilian', role:'general|staff|regimental|private|civilian', written_year, lag_years, genre:'official_report|memoir|testimony|address|periodical', bias_tags:['lost_cause','controversy:Longstreet-Allan','partisan_committee_1864']}. Segment B&L by contents (title/author/page), SHSP by article with Gettysburg-density scoring (>= N mentions/1,000 words) then human shortlist (~150), Joint Committee by witness. UI rule: answers that cite tagged passages must show a 'perspective' chip and, for controversy tags, at least one opposing-side passage.
plan_items.acceptance_test: 100% of narrative passages carry perspective+lag fields; SHSP shortlist reviewed (>=150 articles) with reviewer initials; a test question about Longstreet's July 2 delay returns passages from >= 2 sides with visible chips.

plan_items.title: Extract ~5,400 clock-time expressions and dated dispatches from the OR and use them as ground-truth time anchors to reconcile the site's timeline (C4)
plan_items.evidence: Regex count over OR text (heuristic; includes false positives): 2,269 clock-time expressions in Pt1, 947 in Pt2, 2,204 in Pt3 (total 5,420); 225 'July 1-3, 1863' date strings in Pt3. OR27-1 also holds the Itinerary (No.7) and IA itineraryofarmy00united (80 imgs, NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT). Audit C4 lists data labels such as Longstreet 7:30am, Vincent 8:25am, Pickett's Charge 11:05am vs history ~4pm/4:30pm/3pm; BRIEF time-facts CSVs exist in plan-work.
plan_items.root_cause: The timeline was authored from memory/secondary summaries; no machine-checkable anchor set exists, so contradictions (dusk at 12:10pm) survive.
plan_items.fix: time_anchors.py: regex grammar for (\d{1,2})(?:[:.](\d{2}))?\s*(?:o.clock)?\s*([ap])\.?\s?m\b, 'noon', 'daybreak', 'sunset', 'dusk', 'about/near/before/after' modifiers; attach to nearest preceding event sentence with unit + place via alias table + gazetteer (SRC-23). Output time_anchors.jsonl {anchor_id, source_ref, unit_id, place, date (July 1-3), time_text, time_min (local minutes since midnight), modifier, confidence, quote}. Timezone note: OR times are local mean/sun time; store +/-10 min tolerance. Then diff against chronology_day*.json event times and the 675-tick clock and emit a discrepancy CSV (event, site_time, anchor_median, n_anchors, IQR).
plan_items.acceptance_test: >= 3,000 anchors parsed with unit or place tag; precision >= 90% on a 200-anchor hand-labelled sample; discrepancy CSV covers all 137 chronology events with n_anchors and median; the 8 flagged C4 examples each show >= 2 independent anchors.
plan_items.metric_or_grade_moved: Historical accuracy (C4); enables honest 'reported times' UI

plan_items.title: Georeference LoC Bachelder (1876/1883/1863) and Warren maps; locate the reported 28 time-stamped Bachelder maps (NARA RG 77 / GNMP) before digitising troop positions
plan_items.evidence: LoC items verified via ?fo=json: 99447491 (Bachelder 1876, 3 sheets, 1:12,000, topography engraved by Julia Bien, positions by L.E. Neuman), 99447492 (1883 ed.), 99448794 (Warren, from the Jubal Early Collection, 'base for Bachelder'), 93517377 (1863 isometrical), 99448798/99448799 (Woeltje & Cutting 1888 with landowner names). IIIF info.json verified 200 at tile.loc.gov (first-day sheet 12.5% render = 1,036x1,344 px). LoC G&M rights: 'free to use and reuse unless a Rights Advisory statement is present'. NARA blog (fetched) lists 5 RG 77 Gettysburg maps with NAIDs (305570, 17370358, 6860337, 102279222, 176246316, 176246318). Dealer pages describe 28 hourly Bachelder maps - not verified in any repository I could read.
plan_items.root_cause: The map has no historically georeferenced base or troop-position layer; positions/timing come from memory-based placement files.
plan_items.fix: 1) Pull item JSON + IIIF info.json for the 8 LoC items (<= 20 requests/min; cache). 2) Georeference Warren first (25-40 GCPs: road intersections, Codori/Trostle/Weikert buildings, Seminary, cemetery gates; thin-plate spline; RMS < 15 m) in Allmaps or QGIS; then Bachelder sheets to Warren. 3) Publish PMTiles/raster tiles as an optional 'Historic map' overlay with Library of Congress credit line. 4) Ask NARA Cartographic (College Park) and GNMP archivist whether the 28 hourly maps exist digitally; if yes they become the top-priority placement source. 5) Only then digitise Bachelder symbols to GeoJSON (day, position class first/intermediate/evening, unit_id).
plan_items.acceptance_test: Warren + 3 Bachelder sheets georeferenced with RMS < 15 m and 10 independent check points < 25 m; overlay toggle renders at z12-17 without console errors; NARA/GNMP inquiry answered in writing (yes/no + access route); attribution string matches LoC credit line.
plan_items.metric_or_grade_moved: Content depth; placement accuracy (D3); feeds C4 spatial checks

plan_items.title: Curate 40-75 rights-gated LoC photographs (Gardner/O'Sullivan/Gibson, July 5-7 1863 aftermath) for the Historian and Ground Remembers pages
plan_items.evidence: LoC collection API civil-war-glass-negatives q=gettysburg returns 185 records (4 pages of 50); 75 have created_published containing '1863 July.'; contributors O'Sullivan 34, Gardner 31, Gibson 15, Smith 15. Rights: 118 records carry 'No known restrictions on publication. For information, see "Civil war photographs, 1861-1865," https://www.loc.gov/rr/print/res/120_cwar.html', 55 carry 'No known restrictions on publication.', 12 carry none; 3 have a 1917 'Copyright J224990' note (studio copy prints). LoC title flags misattribution: 'Dead Confederate sharpshooter at foot of Little Round Top [i.e., Devil's Den]'.
plan_items.root_cause: No period imagery in the Historian; audit S1 found sub-pages that are only a search box.
plan_items.fix: photos.py: paginate with 3-s spacing (JSON limit 20/min); keep id, title, date, contributor, notes, rights_advisory, image_url; rule: accept only rights_advisory startswith 'No known restrictions' AND notes lack 'Copyright'; download service_medium (r.jpg) only for curated ids; convert to AVIF/WebP with 3 widths; store photos.json {lcid, lc_dig_id, caption_loc, caption_site, photographer, date_text, place_key, unit_ids, credit:'Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division, LC-DIG-...'}; label all as 'aftermath (photographed ~July 5-7 or later)' and never attach to battle ticks; add caption-correction notes where LoC notes a correction.
plan_items.acceptance_test: photos.json has >= 40 approved entries each with rights_advisory text stored verbatim and credit line; zero entries with missing rights or 'Copyright' notes; images served <= 150 KB at 800 px with width/height set (no CLS); alt text for all.
plan_items.metric_or_grade_moved: Content richness; accessibility (alt text), CLS if dims set

plan_items.title: Newspapers: curated Chronicling America harvest now; re-OCR The Compiler (Pennsylvania Newspaper Archive) later; open licence talks for the Adams Sentinel
plan_items.evidence: Chronicling America (loc.gov API) returns 1,425 full-text pages mentioning 'gettysburg' for 1863-07-04..07-31 (New-York Daily Tribune 76, New York Herald 69, Chicago Daily Tribune 48, Cleveland Morning Leader 48, Worcester Daily Spy 41, Portland Daily Press 36). No Gettysburg-published 1863 title turned up in CA title queries (Adams Sentinel record sn83032079 is title-level only, digitized False). The Compiler (Gettysburg) 1857-66 IS at panewsarchive.psu.edu (51 issues in 1863; no July 6 issue) but OCR is poor: in-vocabulary proxy 0.43-0.48 on 4 pages of 1863-07-13 vs 0.95-0.98 for IA books; page 2 begins 'BATTLES 0F GETTYSBURG. "Our uguallyquict null unpretnullmg lit tle town of Gettysburg has become hiutnric."'. Adams Sentinel/Star and Banner/Star and Sentinel are 'Newspaper Archive (subscription)' per Gettysburg College libguide.
plan_items.root_cause: Local contemporary voices are absent from the Historian; the free local paper's OCR is unusable as-is.
plan_items.fix: Phase A (M): ca_harvest.py - fixed query list x July 4-15, 1863, facet by title, cache JSON, download OCR for ~200 pages, extract ~50-150 telegram-bulletin articles with headers. Phase B (XL, deferred): re-OCR ~80 Compiler pages (Jul 13-Nov 30) from PNA IIIF images with Tesseract 5/Kraken, LLM post-correction, 10-page gold set to report CER, article segmentation. Phase C (S): email Gettysburg College Special Collections/Musselman Library about research licence for Adams Sentinel 1863.
plan_items.acceptance_test: Phase A: >= 50 cleaned articles with title/date/page/url and rights statement; Phase B: gold-set CER <= 5% and article count report; Phase C: written reply logged in governance register.

plan_items.evidence: npshistory.com/publications/gett/mon-locations-1932.pdf (2,095,190 bytes) has a text layer: pdftotext -layout gives 139,713 chars with rows 'Regiment | Brigade | Corps | Location' by state and arm (e.g. '14 Smyth ... plan_items.title: Licensing governance: per-source rights registry, exclusion list and permission outreach (Ladd/Bachelder Papers, NHHS, Stone Sentinels, NYSMM, Rumsey, Busey & Martin)
plan_items.evidence: IA bachelderpapersg0001unse = Morningside 1994 lending scan (not open). NHHS: 'For permission to reproduce this image, please add the image to your cart and proceed through the Image Request checkout process', fees $25/$50. Stone Sentinels footer '(c)2026 Steve A. Hawks'. NYSMM footer '(c)2026 ... All rights reserved.' Rumsey: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (about page) vs CC BY-NC-SA 2.0 (record page) - inconsistent, non-commercial. IA also hosts non-PD reprints (1971 OR reprint warrebellionaco00cowlgoog; 1959 Dyer).
plan_items.root_cause: A historian feature that quotes text at scale needs an auditable rights basis per passage; today none exists.
plan_items.fix: Add rights.json entries {source_id, status:'PD-US|LoC-no-known-restrictions|permission-required|excluded', basis, statement_text, statement_url, verified_at, reviewer}; enforce in the ingest CLI (refuse sources without rights.status in allow-list); require original-imprint checks (year <= 1930, publisher, not reprint) in the IA fetcher; send permission requests for X-01/X-02/X-03/X-05 (templates in report); publish an /about-sources page listing every source, licence and credit line.
plan_items.acceptance_test: CLI blocks a test run on warrebellionaco00cowlgoog (1971 reprint) and on an item without rights; /about-sources lists 100% of ingested sources with statement URL; permission log has dated entries for NHHS, Ladd/Morningside, Gettysburg College.

plan_items.title: Polite, resumable fetch infrastructure with raw-source cache, manifest and per-host rate limits
plan_items.evidence: Measured behaviour: loc.gov JSON API documented at 20 req/min (1-hour block; image/text 150/min) - HTML item pages and /manifest.json returned HTTP 403 to my script at times while ?fo=json and tile.loc.gov kept working; HathiTrust babel robots.txt 'Disallow: /cgi/' (Crawl-delay 1) + Cloudflare 403; Project Gutenberg 'intended for human users only' (bulk via robot/harvest with wget -w 2) and returned 503/504 intermittently; Pennsylvania Newspaper Archive intermittently times out; Emory-sourced IA items use underscores in file names (01300611_3315_djvu.txt vs id 01300611.3315.emory.edu).
plan_items.root_cause: Each source has different limits, formats and failure modes; ad-hoc scripts will get IPs blocked or silently ingest wrong files.
plan_items.fix: tools/ingest/fetch.py with per-host token buckets (loc.gov 0.3 req/s; archive.org 2 req/s; panewsarchive 0.5 req/s; gutenberg mirror/harvest only; hathitrust: Bib API only), identifying User-Agent with contact email, ETag/If-None-Match caching, sha256 manifest, retry with backoff on 429/5xx, hard-stop on 403 with human-review message, IA helper that reads /metadata to choose files, size guard (skip > 100 MB unless --allow-big), resumable state file.
plan_items.acceptance_test: Dry-run against 20 mixed URLs never exceeds host limits (logged); re-run downloads 0 bytes (304/cache hit); on injected 403 the tool stops and prints remediation; manifest contains sha256, size, fetched_at, source_id for every file.
plan_items.metric_or_grade_moved: Reliability of the data pipeline; enables all ingest items

plan_items.title: OCR quality gates and targeted re-OCR: measure every source, re-OCR the poor ones (Compiler, Confederate Veteran, Gardner captions, Atlas)
plan_items.evidence: Measured in-vocabulary proxy (1.0 best): OR27-1 0.984, OR27-3 0.967, Fox prose 0.977, NY Final Report v1 0.968, Battles&Leaders v3 0.966, Joint Committee 0.960, Phisterer v1 0.943, PA at Gettysburg 0.935-0.949, Clark NC v2 0.933, Maine at Gettysburg 0.892, Bates v1 0.878, Wert 0.867, Confederate Veteran v1 0.835, GNMP 1921 list 0.829, Atlas 0.685, Compiler 1863-07-13 0.43-0.48, Gardner Sketch Book 0.046 (image-only).
plan_items.root_cause: OCR quality varies by an order of magnitude; without a gate, garbled text enters embeddings and quotes.
plan_items.fix: ocr_gate.py: compute proxy per document/section against the growing vocabulary; thresholds: >= 0.90 auto-accept; 0.80-0.90 accept with spell-repair and flag; < 0.80 quarantine for re-OCR. For quarantined sources download page images (IA JP2 zip or PNA IIIF) and re-OCR with Tesseract 5 (lang eng, --psm 1/4 column-aware) or Kraken; keep both texts with an 'ocr_engine' field. Add numeric-table validators (row sums) for Fox and casualty returns.
plan_items.acceptance_test: Every ingested document has ocr_score; documents < 0.80 never reach the retrieval index; re-OCR raises the Compiler sample proxy above 0.85 on a 10-page gold set.

plan_items.title: Page-accurate citation model (IA leaf -> printed page -> deep link) for every quoted passage
plan_items.evidence: IA *_page_numbers.json for warofrebellion271unit maps 1,188 leaves to printed pages (leaf 401 -> '383', leaf 703 -> '683'); *_djvu.txt has NO form-feed page markers (0 found), so page boundaries need *_djvu.xml (46.6 MB, one <OBJECT> per leaf) or running-head regex; Chamberlain report starts OR p.622 (Part 1, leaf ~640). HathiTrust deep links are babel.hathitrust.org/cgi/pt?id=coo.31924077699761;seq=N (HTML blocked to scripts but fine for human links).
plan_items.root_cause: Without page mapping the Historian can cite only 'Official Records' rather than 'OR Ser. I, vol. 27, pt. 1, p. 623', so answers are unverifiable.
plan_items.fix: For each IA item stream-parse djvu.xml (lxml.iterparse) to get text per leaf, join with page_numbers.json to get printed page (fill gaps by interpolation), store leaf and printed_page on every chunk; generate two deep links per citation: archive.org/details/<id>?view=theater&ui=embed#page/n<leaf>/mode/1up and the Hathi seq link when an htid mapping exists (Bib API). Citation formatter: 'OR, Ser. I, vol. 27, pt. 1, p. 623 (Chamberlain, 20th Maine)'.
plan_items.acceptance_test: 100 random chunks: printed page matches the scan in 98+; citation strings render for 100% of chunks; links open the right page for 20 manual checks.

plan_items.title: Close source-coverage gaps: Wisconsin, Massachusetts, Delaware, New Hampshire, West Virginia, Confederate state monument commissions; outreach for Bachelder holdings
plan_items.evidence: IA title searches found no Gettysburg commission volume for WI/MA/DE/NH/WV; UW-Madison catalog record 'Report of Commissioners to Care for Gettysburg Battle Monuments, 1892' exists (digital status unverified); Wisconsin Historical Society holds monument photographs. Site units: WI 6, MA 18, NH 3, DE 2, WV 4. No digital 'Bachelder Project', NYS Library or Gettysburg College Bachelder collection was found (NHHS holds the physical papers: 10 boxes + 7 volumes; finding aid PDF verified).
plan_items.root_cause: Some states never published a single commission volume online (or it is not on IA); Confederate states mostly memorialised after 1900.
plan_items.fix: Workaround coverage matrix: WI via OR Nos.34-36 (Mansfield/Dawes/Robinson), Curtis, Haskell, Wisconsin History Commission Reprints No.1; MA via Roe 1910 + OR + B&L; Confederate via OR Pt2 + Clark + CMH + SHSP + Polley/Oates. Email UW-Madison/WHS for scan status; ask NHHS for item-level quote/permission for ~10 targeted Bachelder letters.
plan_items.acceptance_test: Coverage report lists per state: units, sources available, sources missing; outreach log has dated entries; each gap has a stated workaround.

plan_items.title: Source-level QA harness: 100-passage random audit per source plus a 25-question retrieval gold set
plan_items.evidence: Audit H8: 'why did Lee lose the war' returned Pickett + 'Archer Captured'; long vignettes dumped as walls of text. historian.html:48 promises every answer 'traces back to a real row of data'.
plan_items.root_cause: No evaluation exists to show that new sources improve answers rather than add noise.
plan_items.fix: Create eval/gold.yaml with 25 questions across unit facts (20th Maine commander/position), time (when did Pickett's Charge begin), causation (Lee's July 3 decision), bias (Longstreet at Gettysburg), place (Peach Orchard), each with accepted source ids + page. Per source, sample 100 passages, check text fidelity vs scan, unit link correctness, license flag; report pass rate in CI. Track recall@5 and citation-precision before/after each source is added.
plan_items.acceptance_test: Each source has a QA report >= 95% pass; gold-set recall@5 >= 0.8 and citation precision >= 0.9 after P0 sources; regressions fail CI.

plan_items.title: Corpus size and hosting budget for P0/P1 sources (raw ~75 MB P0 text; 20-50k chunks) to inform retrieval architecture
plan_items.evidence: Measured raw OCR sizes: OR27 11.26 MB (3.97+3.88+3.41), Battles&Leaders v3 3.27 MB, SHSP v1-43 49.0 MB, NY Final Report v1 1.44 MB (vols 2-3 ~1.5-1.7 MB each), PA at Gettysburg ~2 MB/volume, Fox 2.26 MB, Clark NC ~1.8-2.2 MB/vol, Phisterer 3.6-3.9 MB/vol, Dyer 14.7 MB, Bates 6.6-9.1 MB/vol. P0 raw (OR + B&L + SHSP + NY + PA + Fox) ~= 75 MB; Gettysburg-filtered SHSP would shrink 49 MB to a few MB.
plan_items.root_cause: Site is static Netlify hosting; retrieval design (client-side vs edge vs hybrid) depends on corpus size.
plan_items.fix: Store raw in a private bucket or repo LFS (not in the deploy); publish only derived, filtered passages (~30 MB, est. 20-50k chunks of ~250 words) as sharded JSON/JSONL + a compact BM25 index, embeddings computed offline and shipped as a quantised binary if a semantic tier is chosen; keep any LLM tier server-side. Coordinate with the retrieval-architecture agent.
plan_items.acceptance_test: Budget doc lists bytes per shard, gzip/brotli sizes, chunk counts; initial route payload for the Historian stays < 150 KB (index shards lazy-loaded).
plan_items.metric_or_grade_moved: Performance (LCP/INP) of the Historian page; hosting cost
